english.title: Send / attempt to send false / misleading message likely to endanger safety of person / ship / aircraft / vehicle
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[sent,]_
(B)_[attempted to send,]_

by means of wireless telegraphy, a message, which to your knowledge was false or misleading and was likely to

(C)_[prejudice the efficiency of a safety of life service]_
(D)_[endanger the safety of a person]_
(E)_[endanger the safety of a ship]_
(F)_[endanger the safety of an aircraft]_
(G)_[endanger the safety of a vehicle]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 47 of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) Section 47(3) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 provides that this applies in particular to a message which, to the person's knowledge, falsely suggests that a ship or aircraft is in distress or in need of assistance; or is not in distress or not in need of assistance.
(ii) Section 105 of the Act makes special provisions for this offence in relation to ships and aircraft.
(iii) Section 107 of the Act provides for proceedings and enforcement regarding this offence.
(iv) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022, see paragraph 16 of Schedule 8 to the Act; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 35(2)(a) of the Act and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
